title: I made a tilt game with Claude Code, and the bot in it is scripted, not AI
author: freechoice
selftext:
I made a game while sitting on a toilet, and Claude Code agents wrote and reviewed most of the code. I am the dev, and I direct them.

Tiltanic is a tilt game: a tiny steamboat rides a sloshing sea through gates. Agents wrote the code that draws the art and makes the music. Play it free in the browser, no signup and no install: [https://tiltanic.com/](https://tiltanic.com/?s=reddit-aigamedev&c=post1)

For one big release I cut the work into 16 packages. A Sonnet agent builds each one in its own git worktree. A fresh Opus agent, which did not write the code, reviews it. A lead agent merges. Three reviews ended with "merge after lead fix", so the review was not a rubber stamp.

My part is the decisions: 36 numbered ones are on file, like "one share button". I also do what an agent cannot: test on a real phone, run the deploy that touches AWS, and post.

What did not work: real devices. The tilt code has 21 fake-browser cases, not a device farm, and agents alone wrote and checked the 13 translations.

One lesson: log every deviation from the spec, with a reason. My build log holds 78. It is a cheap way to see what an agent really did.

The bot that races you is a scripted planner, not AI. It tries 49 short tilt plans and keeps the safest. A script plays it offline into files for 450 days, so the phone plans nothing.

Do you let your agent write the art code too, or only the game logic?
